**Shin Hae-chul** (Korean:신해철; May 6, 1968 – October 27, 2014)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-:1-1) was a South Korean singer-songwriter and the frontman, vocalist of rock band N.EX.T. He was a record producer known for being a pioneer of Korean experimental rock music. He was referred to by fans as the "Demon Lord" or "The Devil" for his charismatic stage presence.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-3)

Shin and his band Muhangwedo debuted at the 1988 MBC Campus Music Festival, where the band won first place for the song "To You."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-:0-4) He formed the experimental rock band N.EX.T in 1992.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-5) He was also known for hosting a radio show from 2001 to 2012.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-:0-4)
Shin died as a result of medical malpractice after undergoing surgery in 2014.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-6)
Shin Hae-chul was born on May 6, 1968.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-:1-1) He enrolled in Sogang University in 1987, where he studied philosophy until he dropped out to focus on his music career.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-:2-7)
Shin formed the band Muhangwedo (무한궤도) in 1988 when he was a sophomore at Sogang University. The band received national attention when it appeared on the televised 1988 MBC Campus Music Festival, a singing competition for amateurs. Muhangwedo won first place for the song "To You" (그대에게) which was written by Shin.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-:2-7) The band released one album, 1989's _When Our Lives Are Almost Over_ (우리 앞의 생이 끝나갈 때).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-8)

Shin released his first solo album in 1990, which included a song that had an English rap, which was unconventional in the Korean music scene at the time. The album was a huge hit, leading to Shin rising to the top of Korean pop music charts and receiving multiple Korean pop music awards. His second solo album, _Myself_, was released in 1991, which was first album in Korea to have used midi. He also started a gig as a radio DJ on MBC FM.
In 1992, Shin formed the band N.EX.T — moving from pop music to rock. Their first album, _Home_, was a concept album. While his previous songs were mainly about love or heartache, here Shin started to write more about social issues, such as criticizing the fast lifestyle of urbanites in "City People". The group's second album was released in 1994 titled _The Return of N.EX.T Part 1: The Being_ where Shin introduced more philosophical lyrics, such as questioning the meaning of life in the song "The Ocean: About Immortality". The band's third album, _The Return of N.EX.T Part 2: World_. Some of the band members changed over time, with Shin being the constant lead singer/songwriter.
During this time he also did a one-time collaboration with singer Yoon Sang to form Nodance, wrote the original sound track for the Korean movie _Jungle Story_, and was the DJ for the MBC FM radio program _FM Music City_ from 1996 to 1997. In 1996, he created his own label, Big Bang Music.
In 1997 N.EX.T released a rock ballad single, "Here, I Stand for You" which sold 500,000 copies in South Korea. The band went on to release their fourth album _Lazenca: A Space Rock Opera_ in November 1997, which was also the original sound track for the television animation series _Lazenca_. The band split up after this- Shin went on to study music producing in London.

In London, Shin re-named himself Crom (inspired by Cromwell) and released a techno album _Crom's Techno Works_ in 1998. The following year, he formed a project group Monocrom with guitarist Chris Tsangarides and released the eponymous project album _Monocrom_. The music in the album was experimental, combining heavy metal with Korean folk music, rap, and lyrical rock ballads. Most of the songs in this album were in English, which he collaborated with lyricist D. Yvette Wohn. After the release of _Monocrom_, Shin went to New York where he worked on producing his live album and some Korean movie soundtracks. In 2000, he created a three-man band Wittgenstein to produce a home studio album of the same name. He also wrote the song "Zergs are Coming" for the StarCraft music album.
Shin returned to Korea in 2002 and worked on various projects, mainly writing songs for other artists or for movie soundtracks. In 2004, he re-formed the group N.EX.T although the members were different, and released a double album _The Return of N.EX.T Part 3: 개한민국_. He also started DJing for a late night radio show _Ghost Nation_ that became extremely popular. In 2007, N.EX.T released a jazz album _The Songs for the One_ inspired by his newborn daughter. In 2008, the band released the album _666 Trilogy_. After a long break, the band's final album, _Reboot Myself_ was released in 2014.
In 2004, Shin participated in a special project with the best musicians of Korea, an album named "Tribute to Park Nohae's Collection of poems _The Dawn of Labor_ 20th anniversary".[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-10) It is the first attempted project in the history of Korean music with recordings dedicated to poetry. Shin sang "Heaven" (하늘) with Psy on this album.

Throughout his career Shin hosted several radio programs, including _Music City with Shin Hae Chul_[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-11) and _GhostStation with Shin Hae Chul_[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-12) After supporting and campaigning for the president Roh Moo-hyun in 2002 election, Mr. Shin hosts the popular _Ghost Nation_ on MBC, a late-night radio program since 2003. His fans call him "Mawang" (마왕 'the Demon Lord').
On September 16, 2007, Shin ended _Ghost Nation_, but he also announced that the show would be broadcast on the internet and no longer through MBC.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-13)
He married Yoon Won-hee (윤원희) on September 29, 2002,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-14) just before the 2002 election. He released his first jazz album _The Songs for the One_ in 2007, dedicated to his wife and daughter.
Shin was found to be suffering from prosopagnosia, on a TV show (_MBC Goldfish_) in which he made a guest appearance.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-15) After that, he hosted a brand-new TV comedy debate program _100-second Debate_ (since May 2007), with a similar format of the MBC's _100 Minute Debate_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-16) On July 29, 2007, he appeared as a victim (guest) of Lee Kyung-kyu's _Hidden Camera_.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-17)

Shin was treated for gastrointestinal problems by Dr. Kang Se-hoon at Sky Hospital on October 17, 2014.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-:3-18)_[unreliable source?_] Kang carried out stomach reduction surgery without consent from Shin.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-:3-18) During surgery, Kang punctured Shin's upper small intestine and pericardium, which later resulted in peritonitis. After developing a fever, which he was told was normal after surgery, Shin suffered a heart attack on October 22, and died on October 27 from peritonitis, pericarditis, sepsis, and brain damage due to lack of oxygen.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-:3-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-:4-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-20) At the urging of friends, Shin's family stopped his cremation at short notice and requested an autopsy.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-21) In March 2015, Songpa police found that Shin Hae-chul died from medical malpractice.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-22) Kang was struck off the medical register, fined and sentenced to one year in jail.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-:4-19) The death of Shin through malpractice led to a revision of the law in South Korea to allow a state-run agency to help in malpractice cases. The law is referred to as the "Shin Hae-chul Law."[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-23)

Shin's remains were cremated on Seoul Memorial Park in Wonji-dong on November 4th and placed in a columbarium at Utopia Memorial Park in Anseong the following day.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-24) In October 2015, they moved the remains to a pyramidal grave inspired by one of his daughter's drawings.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-27)
Psy's song "Dream" was released in 2015 as a tribute to Shin, donating the profits to his bereaved family. The lyrics recount conversations Psy had with Shin while he was still alive.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-29)
On the fourteenth episode of _Hangout with Yoo_, Yoo Jae-suk played drums, as part of the show format, to accompany the unreleased song "Father and I: Part 3". The song used the pre-recorded vocal narrated monologue of Shin Hae-chul, and was supported by his friend and colleague, Lee Seung-hwan, and fan, Ha Hyun-woo. The new version was called "Stargazer" by Lee Seung-hwan. It was played to and lauded by some of the biggest names in the Korean music industry, all of whom took a moment to praise the genius nature of Shin._[citation needed_]

## Shin Hae-chul's Music Career
### Radio DJ Work
Throughout his career, Shin hosted several radio programs. These included _Music City with Shin Hae Chul_ and _GhostStation with Shin Hae Chul_. Since 2003, Mr. Shin hosted the popular _Ghost Nation_ on MBC. This was a late-night radio program. His fans often called him "Mawang" (마왕), which means 'the Demon Lord'.
On September 16, 2007, Shin ended _Ghost Nation_ on MBC. However, he announced that the show would continue online.

## Personal Life
Shin married Yoon Won-hee (윤원희) on September 29, 2002. He released his first jazz album _The Songs for the One_ in 2007. He dedicated this album to his wife and daughter.
Shin also appeared on a TV show (MBC Goldfish) where it was discovered he had prosopagnosia. This is a condition where a person has difficulty recognizing faces. After that, he hosted a new TV comedy debate program called _100-second Debate_. This show was similar to MBC's _100 Minute Debate_.

## Personal Life
### Shin Hae-chul's Passing
Shin went to Sky Hospital for stomach problems on October 17, 2014. During surgery, the doctor accidentally caused injuries to Shin's small intestine and heart sac. This led to a serious infection. Shin developed a fever, but he was told it was normal after surgery. On October 22, he had a heart attack. He sadly passed away on October 27. The cause was a severe infection and brain damage from lack of oxygen.
At the suggestion of his friends, Shin's family stopped his cremation. They asked for an autopsy to find out what happened. In March 2015, the police found that Shin Hae-chul died due to medical mistakes. The doctor involved was punished and sentenced to jail. Shin's death led to a new law in South Korea. This law helps people in cases of medical mistakes. It is known as the "Shin Hae-chul Law."

## Personal Life
### Tributes to Shin Hae-chul
Psy's song "Dream" was released in 2015 as a tribute to Shin. The lyrics were based on talks they had about life and death. Psy said he would donate the money from this song to Shin's family.

### Doctor suspected of resulting in musician's death pleads not guilty
#### Also indicted for misappropriation of business secrets, violation of medical law
Nearly two-and-a-half years have passed since Shin Hae-chul, one of the nation’s most famous pop musicians, died from a medical accident, but it seems unlikely his fans will soon know exactly where the responsibility lies.
In the first hearing of the appeals trial Thursday, Kang Se-hoon, the doctor who was convicted in a lower court on a charge of professional negligence resulting in death, pleaded not guilty. Prosecutors also indicted Kang for the misappropriation of business secrets and violation of medical law. The first trial found him not guilty on the latter two charges, however.
Kang is suspected of conducting a stomach surgery on Shin without the latter’s consent, accidentally puncturing his small intestine and pericardium and causing the peritonitis and blood poisoning, which killed the star singer in October 2014.
Shin reportedly complained of chest pain after undergoing intestinal surgery at Sky Hospital in southern Seoul and died of heart failure a few days later. Kang is also accused of failing to take proper measures after the singer complained of continued pain.
Prosecutors said Kang ignored the danger signs, such as abdominal swelling and a high white blood cell count. All Kang did was prescribing painkillers and telling him to put up with the pain, according to lawyers representing the victim's family.
Kang Se-hoon speaks at an appeals court Thursday, defending himself from a charge of professional negligence resulting in the death of musician Shin Hae-chul in 2014.
After Shin had died, Kang closed the hospital but opened a new hospital later and has continued his obesity metabolic surgery.
The Ministry of Health and Welfare, after receiving complaints about complications and other problems from other patients, has ordered Kang to discontinue the obesity metabolic surgery based on Provision 1, Article 59, of the Medical Law.
The first trial judges sentenced Kang to eight months in jail with a stay of execution for two years while maintaining Kang’s license. Both the prosecution and Kang appealed the ruling.

### Doctor suspected of resulting in musician's death pleads not guilty
#### Also indicted for misappropriation of business secrets, violation of medical law
The prosecution has pointed out in the petition statement that there is a legal misunderstanding on the part of the judiciary regarding the charges of business secret leaks and violations of the medical law, and the penalty for the accidental homicide was too lenient, given the nature of the crime.
Kang's attorney struck back, saying, "Shin’s death is due to his failure to follow the doctor’s instruction on hospitalization, and so Kang does not deserve what happened to his patient.”
The judges also questioned Kang about the cardiac puncture, the cause of Shin's death.
Kang reiterated his advice – or instruction – for Shin to stay at the hospital and undergo checkups, which the latter did not follow.
Lawyers for Shin, however, stressed the late musician did not content to the stomach surgery in the first place, pointing out that there were two more victims, including an Australian, for similar reasons.
Experts said the legal battle would likely go on for some time, but the medical community will need to seriously consider drawing a clearer line between the rights of patients and their doctors, including how much can be excused under the doctors’ arbitrary and unproven surgical procedure in the name of bona fide intention.
The next trial will be on April 20.

### Doctor suspected of resulting in musician's death pleads not guilty
#### Also indicted for misappropriation of business secrets, violation of medical law
Nearly two-and-a-half years have passed since Shin Hae-chul, one of the nation’s most famous pop musicians, died from a medical accident, but it seems unlikely his fans will soon know exactly where the responsibility lies.
In the first hearing of the appeals trial Thursday, Kang Se-hoon, the doctor who was convicted in a lower court on a charge of professional negligence resulting in death, pleaded not guilty. Prosecutors also indicted Kang for the misappropriation of business secrets and violation of medical law. The first trial found him not guilty on the latter two charges, however.
Kang is suspected of conducting a stomach surgery on Shin without the latter’s consent, accidentally puncturing his small intestine and pericardium and causing the peritonitis and blood poisoning, which killed the star singer in October 2014.
Shin reportedly complained of chest pain after undergoing intestinal surgery at Sky Hospital in southern Seoul and died of heart failure a few days later. Kang is also accused of failing to take proper measures after the singer complained of continued pain.
Prosecutors said Kang ignored the danger signs, such as abdominal swelling and a high white blood cell count. All Kang did was prescribing painkillers and telling him to put up with the pain, according to lawyers representing the victim's family.
Kang Se-hoon speaks at an appeals court Thursday, defending himself from a charge of professional negligence resulting in the death of musician Shin Hae-chul in 2014.
After Shin had died, Kang closed the hospital but opened a new hospital later and has continued his obesity metabolic surgery.
The Ministry of Health and Welfare, after receiving complaints about complications and other problems from other patients, has ordered Kang to discontinue the obesity metabolic surgery based on Provision 1, Article 59, of the Medical Law.
The first trial judges sentenced Kang to eight months in jail with a stay of execution for two years while maintaining Kang’s license. Both the prosecution and Kang appealed the ruling.

A case in which South Korean singer Shin Hae -cheol died due to a medical accident caused by doctor Kang Se-hoon . It is considered **the worst medical accident case in the history of the Republic of Korea** , and is subject to the Act on Medical Accident Damage Relief and Medical Dispute Mediation, etc.[[4]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%8B%A0%ED%95%B4%EC%B2%A0%20%EC%9D%98%EB%A3%8C%EC%82%AC%EA%B3%A0%20%EC%82%AC%EB%A7%9D%EC%82%AC%EA%B1%B4#fn-4) It became the background for its enactment.

## 1.outline
Shin Hae-chul in 2009 Suffering from symptoms of reflux esophagitis, he visited Seoul Sky Hospital, where the accident would occur a few years later, and underwent a gastric banding procedure at the doctor's recommendation. # In 2012, Shin Hae-chul underwent surgery to remove the gastric band at the aforementioned Seoul Sky Hospital.[[5]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%8B%A0%ED%95%B4%EC%B2%A0%20%EC%9D%98%EB%A3%8C%EC%82%AC%EA%B3%A0%20%EC%82%AC%EB%A7%9D%EC%82%AC%EA%B1%B4#fn-5)[[6]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%8B%A0%ED%95%B4%EC%B2%A0%20%EC%9D%98%EB%A3%8C%EC%82%AC%EA%B3%A0%20%EC%82%AC%EB%A7%9D%EC%82%AC%EA%B1%B4#fn-6) , complications of intestinal stenosis in 2014[[7]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%8B%A0%ED%95%B4%EC%B2%A0%20%EC%9D%98%EB%A3%8C%EC%82%AC%EA%B3%A0%20%EC%82%AC%EB%A7%9D%EC%82%AC%EA%B1%B4#fn-7) Therefore, the patient underwent the surgery at the relevant hospital on October 17 , was declared brain dead at Asan Medical Center on October 22, and was pronounced dead five days later on October 27. During this process, the attending physicianKang Se-hoon performed gastric plication surgery to fold and reduce the stomach without the consent of the patient (Shin Hae-chul) or his family, and even when the patient complained of pain after the surgery, he claimed it was a normal phenomenon to take after surgery and did not take any follow-up measures.

## 1.outline
As a result, various controversies regarding medical malpractice arose following Shin Hae-chul's death .
From the day of his death **, various rumors** ranging **from****a medical accident****to****an assassination****were spread** on the Internet . His wife, Yoon Won-hee, claimed that **additional surgery was performed without the consent of Shin Hae-cheol and his family** during the surgery . # All medical records were secured by the bereaved family. #
Although cremation was originally planned, the wife, Yoon Won-hee, filed a complaint with the Seoul Songpa Police Station after concluding that there was medical malpractice based on recommendations for an autopsy from fellow singers, a strong response from the agency, and medical records secured by the bereaved family .Fellow celebrities held an emergency briefing and announced that they would halt the scheduled cremation procedure and request an autopsy from the National Forensic Service .

## 2.investigation process
### 2.1.Record of discovery of perforation in the small intestine
According to an SBS NEWS report, a 1cm perforation was discovered in the small intestine during emergency surgery at Asan Medical Center prior to death , and inflammation was also recorded. Given that there are numerous cases of death due to small intestine perforation during laparoscopic surgery simply by searching online, it is all too obvious how far the repercussions will spread if the cause of death is determined to be inflammation resulting from the perforation during an autopsy.
There is also a theory that if the pancreas (pancreas) , not the small intestine, is touched, pancreatic juice leaks and the organ melts like soap, a so-called 'saponification phenomenon', causing a perforation in the small intestine .

## 2.investigation process
### 2.5.National Forensic Service delivers autopsy results to police
The reason Asan Medical Center responded in that manner is that the attending surgeon attempted to shift the blame to the hospital, and the statement is merely a declaration asserting that the hospital's doctors are not at fault. Although the Act on Relief for Victims of Medical Accidents and Mediation of Medical Disputes was submitted to the NationalAssembly , its future has become uncertain as the Korean Medical Association opposes it, citing reasons such as the rise in defensive medicine, increased social costs resulting from lengthy pre-litigation processes, and the deepening avoidance of specialties with a high potential for medical disputes, such as obstetrics and gynecology and cardiovascular and thoracic surgery . While it is said that this is the reason why the indictment rate for major medical accidents in South Korea is only 1%, the actual reason for the low indictment rate is that it is difficult to attribute every medical accident solely to the negligence of the medical staff.
However, it is difficult for the patient to distinguish whether it was the medical staff's fault, bad luck, or the patient acting against medical advice, so many cases are filed even for cases that should not be prosecuted. The rate of incidents that occur decreases accordingly.

## 2.investigation process
### 2.6.Seoul Sky Hospital's application for court management
Kang Se-hoon on his way to Seoul Songpa Police Station for questioning The director of Seoul Sky Hospital made no particular comments, aside from briefly saying "yes" in response to the reporters' question asking if he intended to apologize to the bereaved family.
Afterwards, on December 4, 2014, Seoul Sky Hospital applied for court receivership of the hospital, claiming that due to this incident, the number of patients decreased and doctors left the hospital and were on the verge of bankruptcy. According to Director Kang, the company is under pressure from 9 billion won in debt, and all 50 billion won worth of investment attraction has been lost. # It is said that a bankruptcy attorney has already been appointed and related documents have been prepared.
There is an opinion that the hospital's claim is that it is intended to claim damages as a result of litigation with the bereaved family. In addition, if Director Kang's bankruptcy application is accepted, Director Kang's assets will be frozen so that creditors can be repaid first and his debt will be reduced, so it will inevitably affect the civil lawsuit for compensation of the bereaved family. Even if you win a difficult medical lawsuit, it may be difficult to receive compensation.

## 3.investigation and trial process
### 3.1.Investigation process and first trial
March 3, 2015 As it was revealed that the cause of Shin Hae-chul 's death was medical malpractice, he was referred to the prosecution on charges of negligent homicide .
The police said that gastric rhinoplasty, a gastric reduction surgery without consent, did not directly lead to death, but regarded the resulting perforation and subsequent actions as a medical accident . The perforation that occurred in the small intestine and heart was a delayed perforation, and although the white blood cell count soared to 15,000, post-operative complications were overlooked and an opportunity to save him was missed. In response, the Korean Medical Association and the Korea Medical Dispute Coordination Arbitration Agency said, " I did not recognize that it was an emergency even though the symptoms of peritonitis were in progress. "
Regarding the claim that Director Kang Se-hoon may have violated his fasting order, the police stated that it was only the director's claim and had no basis. Above all, the problem arose from the doctor's attitude of trying to reassure the patient by explaining that the current situation was a normal process after treatment. "Director Kang did not actively identify the cause and treat the patient without diagnosing the situation, which had already passed the peritonitis stage and had already reached the stage of sepsis . ### 3.1.Investigation process and first trial
On May 6, Shin Hae-cheol's birthday, his wife appeared at the prosecution as a reference and was interrogated for seven hours. # He stated the situation before and after the surgery and refuted Director Kang’s claims that he left without permission and violated fasting measures.

Shin Hae-chul's side replaced the lawyer with a doctor-turned-lawyer. #
The prosecution concluded that the cause of Shin Hae-cheol's death was medical negligence and indicted Director Kang on charges of professional negligence causing death. # It was confirmed that Shin Hae-cheol's bereaved family initially filed a complaint against Director Kang, not on charges of professional negligence causing death, but on charges of manslaughter. #
At the first trial held at the Seoul Eastern District Court on October 21, 2015, Director Kang, who performed Shin Hae-cheol's surgery, stated that the hospital was still open for business and that he would refuse a public participation trial. #
Meanwhile, on 'Midnight of TV Entertainment', which aired on October 21, 2015, it was reported that the existing hospital had closed down and the building had been leased out, and the surgeon at the time had moved the hospital to a nearby building and opened for business. Please give us your contact information and we will contact you." #

### 3.2.2nd trial
The 11th Criminal Division of the Seoul Eastern District Court (Chief Judge Ha Hyeon-guk) held the second trial of Director Kang, who was indicted on charges of professional negligence manslaughter, at 3 p.m. on November 18, 2015. Director Kang again denied the charge that he performed gastric reduction surgery without Shin Hae-cheol's consent and caused perforation.
In particular, in response to the prosecution's claim that "the perforation appears to have occurred after laparoscopic surgery" regarding the timing of the perforation, Director Kang responded, "The perforation did not occur during the surgical process, but a delayed perforation that occurred naturally due to the weakening of the inner wall due to the ablative surgery." “It cannot be concluded that this occurrence itself is medical negligence,” he argued. #
He also said, "We are managing it by reducing it from a hospital to a clinic," and added, "We have currently applied for a second rehabilitation and are currently under legal management by the Seoul District Court." Director Kang was also asked, "Are you operating in the same location?" and answered, "We used to use an 8-story stand-alone building, but now we are operating on a smaller scale by renting one floor of a building 500 meters away from the hospital." #
Also, when asked about the discrepancies in the statements of the autopsy doctors, Director Kang replied, "I think the doctors who performed the autopsy made a political decision, not a medical one. Kang, the former director of the Seoul Surgical Hospital in Songpa District of southern Seoul, performed a laparoscopic surgery on Shin after the late singer visited the hospital and complained of a severe stomachache on Oct. 17, 2014. # Shin Hae-chul’s surgeon sentenced to prison
On Tuesday, the Seoul High Court revoked the primary ruling, and sentenced Kang to a full year of imprisonment as opposed to the initial sentence of 10 months of prison and two years probation.
The court also ruled that posting medical information about the patient on the internet is illegal, a charge that the first trial threw out citing that “leaking information about a dead patient is not going against the law.”
“A series of perforations were formed either during or after the surgery performed by the accused,” ruled the court on Jan. 30.
“[The surgeon] should have looked for the cause of the pain if the patient had complained of severe pain after two days of treatment, not prescribe him painkillers. Instead, he didn’t take appropriate measures,” the statement continued.

The reporter tried to interview the director, but received a response from hospital officials saying, "The director is currently undergoing surgery, so we can't do it. Please give us your contact information and we will contact you." #

## 3.investigation and trial process
### 3.2.2nd trial
The 11th Criminal Division of the Seoul Eastern District Court (Chief Judge Ha Hyeon-guk) held the second trial of Director Kang, who was indicted on charges of professional negligence manslaughter, at 3 p.m. on November 18, 2015. Director Kang again denied the charge that he performed gastric reduction surgery without Shin Hae-cheol's consent and caused perforation.
In particular, in response to the prosecution's claim that "the perforation appears to have occurred after laparoscopic surgery" regarding the timing of the perforation, Director Kang responded, "The perforation did not occur during the surgical process, but a delayed perforation that occurred naturally due to the weakening of the inner wall due to the ablative surgery." “It cannot be concluded that this occurrence itself is medical negligence,” he argued. #
He also said, "We are managing it by reducing it from a hospital to a clinic," and added, "We have currently applied for a second rehabilitation and are currently under legal management by the Seoul District Court." Director Kang was also asked, "Are you operating in the same location?" and answered, "We used to use an 8-story stand-alone building, but now we are operating on a smaller scale by renting one floor of a building 500 meters away from the hospital." #
Also, when asked about the discrepancies in the statements of the autopsy doctors, Director Kang replied, "I think the doctors who performed the autopsy made a political decision, not a medical one. There has been no autopsy performed on this type of surgery. That is why there are many medical loopholes in the autopsy results from the National Institute of Forensic Science." #

On Tuesday, the Seoul High Court revoked the primary ruling, and sentenced Kang to a full year of imprisonment as opposed to the initial sentence of 10 months of prison and two years probation.

A South Korean singer-songwriter . He was the leader, frontman, and main vocalist of the rock band N.EX.T.

2. Detail  
Starting with rock music , he attempted a variety of genres of music, from electronica ( techno ), jazz , and Korean traditional music, and made a lot of profound and philosophical songs that were difficult to see in general popular songs by utilizing his major. He was also a all -round musician who wrote , composition , arrangement , and instruments, as well as developing computer programs for producing, engineering and music work. It is also a pioneer and pioneer of Korean computer music (so -called MIDI music). Psy , Seo Tae -ji , and Lee Hyun -do also learned Shin Hae -chul to use samplers and various MIDI music equipment.[37]
From his debut at the 1988 University Festival until his later years, the conclusions of the stories in his songs mostly ended up being cynical, but idealistic messages also coexisted greatly. He often used sex jokes and self-deprecating black humor . Most of the songs released up until the 10th anniversary of his debut are like the above, and between the 10th and 20th anniversaries of his debut, he mixed more direct and aggressive lyrics and humor based on them with the existing serious lyrics.[38] Songs released after 20 years since debut usually contain a lot of self-deprecating humor or black humor aimed at a specific group.

He was nicknamed "Mayor" on FM Music City, a radio program he hosted, and was also nicknamed " The Devil " on Ghost Station , which he hosted later , and among fans . In English, it is usually translated as Demon Lord . However, Shin Hae-cheol's nickname, the devil, was mentioned in an article on page 25 of the Dong-A Ilbo on June 25, 1998, long before Ghost Station.[40] As time passed, the nickname ‘Demon King’ was introduced frequently on terrestrial TV. Even in Internet articles dealing with content that had nothing to do with radio, the expression 'devil' was not missing. In fact, the word ‘demon king’ is no different from Shin Hae-cheol’s pen name.

On the other hand, Shin Hae-cheol has a stage name of Crom, which is derived from Oliver Cromwell , and is a nickname given by engineers instead of his name, which is difficult for foreigners to pronounce, when he was staying in England for the next 4th album~ Monochrome work. So his twitter account is also Crom Shin. At the time, a British engineer said of Shin Hae-chul, 'You must be like Oliver Cromwell when you work with people? This poisonous guy.'
In terms of family relationship, he is the second and youngest of one boy and one girl, and has an older sister who is two years older.[41] Afterwards, Shin Hae-cheol married Yoon Won-hee, a broadcaster from Miss New York, and they also had a son and a daughter. It is also the same in that their children, like themselves, are older sister and younger brother with a two-year gap. (Miss Shin Ha-yeon - Shin Dong-won)

7.6. Cancellation of appointment as editor-in-chief of Maxim

**Shin Hae-chul** (Korean:신해철; May 6, 1968 – October 27, 2014)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-:1-1) was a South Korean singer-songwriter and the frontman, vocalist of rock band N.EX.T. He was a record producer known for being a pioneer of Korean experimental rock music. He was referred to by fans as the "Demon Lord" or "The Devil" for his charismatic stage presence.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-3)

Shin and his band Muhangwedo debuted at the 1988 MBC Campus Music Festival, where the band won first place for the song "To You."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-:0-4) He formed the experimental rock band N.EX.T in 1992.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-5) He was also known for hosting a radio show from 2001 to 2012.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-:0-4)
Shin died as a result of medical malpractice after undergoing surgery in 2014.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-6)
Shin Hae-chul was born on May 6, 1968.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-:1-1) He enrolled in Sogang University in 1987, where he studied philosophy until he dropped out to focus on his music career.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-:2-7)
Shin formed the band Muhangwedo (무한궤도) in 1988 when he was a sophomore at Sogang University. The band received national attention when it appeared on the televised 1988 MBC Campus Music Festival, a singing competition for amateurs. Muhangwedo won first place for the song "To You" (그대에게) which was written by Shin.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-:2-7) The band released one album, 1989's _When Our Lives Are Almost Over_ (우리 앞의 생이 끝나갈 때).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-8)

Shin released his first solo album in 1990, which included a song that had an English rap, which was unconventional in the Korean music scene at the time. The album was a huge hit, leading to Shin rising to the top of Korean pop music charts and receiving multiple Korean pop music awards. His second solo album, _Myself_, was released in 1991, which was first album in Korea to have used midi. He also started a gig as a radio DJ on MBC FM.
In 1992, Shin formed the band N.EX.T — moving from pop music to rock. Their first album, _Home_, was a concept album. While his previous songs were mainly about love or heartache, here Shin started to write more about social issues, such as criticizing the fast lifestyle of urbanites in "City People". The group's second album was released in 1994 titled _The Return of N.EX.T Part 1: The Being_ where Shin introduced more philosophical lyrics, such as questioning the meaning of life in the song "The Ocean: About Immortality". The band's third album, _The Return of N.EX.T Part 2: World_. Some of the band members changed over time, with Shin being the constant lead singer/songwriter.
During this time he also did a one-time collaboration with singer Yoon Sang to form Nodance, wrote the original sound track for the Korean movie _Jungle Story_, and was the DJ for the MBC FM radio program _FM Music City_ from 1996 to 1997. In 1996, he created his own label, Big Bang Music.
In 1997 N.EX.T released a rock ballad single, "Here, I Stand for You" which sold 500,000 copies in South Korea. The band went on to release their fourth album _Lazenca: A Space Rock Opera_ in November 1997, which was also the original sound track for the television animation series _Lazenca_. The band split up after this- Shin went on to study music producing in London.

In London, Shin re-named himself Crom (inspired by Cromwell) and released a techno album _Crom's Techno Works_ in 1998. The following year, he formed a project group Monocrom with guitarist Chris Tsangarides and released the eponymous project album _Monocrom_. The music in the album was experimental, combining heavy metal with Korean folk music, rap, and lyrical rock ballads. Most of the songs in this album were in English, which he collaborated with lyricist D. Yvette Wohn. After the release of _Monocrom_, Shin went to New York where he worked on producing his live album and some Korean movie soundtracks. In 2000, he created a three-man band Wittgenstein to produce a home studio album of the same name. He also wrote the song "Zergs are Coming" for the StarCraft music album.
Shin returned to Korea in 2002 and worked on various projects, mainly writing songs for other artists or for movie soundtracks. In 2004, he re-formed the group N.EX.T although the members were different, and released a double album _The Return of N.EX.T Part 3: 개한민국_. He also started DJing for a late night radio show _Ghost Nation_ that became extremely popular. In 2007, N.EX.T released a jazz album _The Songs for the One_ inspired by his newborn daughter. In 2008, the band released the album _666 Trilogy_. After a long break, the band's final album, _Reboot Myself_ was released in 2014.
In 2004, Shin participated in a special project with the best musicians of Korea, an album named "Tribute to Park Nohae's Collection of poems _The Dawn of Labor_ 20th anniversary".[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-10) It is the first attempted project in the history of Korean music with recordings dedicated to poetry. Shin sang "Heaven" (하늘) with Psy on this album.

**Shin Hae-chul** (Korean:신해철; May 6, 1968 – October 27, 2014)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-:1-1) was a South Korean singer-songwriter and the frontman, vocalist of rock band N.EX.T. He was a record producer known for being a pioneer of Korean experimental rock music. He was referred to by fans as the "Demon Lord" or "The Devil" for his charismatic stage presence.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-3)
texts.1:
Shin and his band Muhangwedo debuted at the 1988 MBC Campus Music Festival, where the band won first place for the song "To You."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-:0-4) He formed the experimental rock band N.EX.T in 1992.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-5) He was also known for hosting a radio show from 2001 to 2012.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-:0-4)
Shin died as a result of medical malpractice after undergoing surgery in 2014.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-6)
Shin Hae-chul was born on May 6, 1968.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-:1-1) He enrolled in Sogang University in 1987, where he studied philosophy until he dropped out to focus on his music career.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-:2-7)
Shin formed the band Muhangwedo (무한궤도) in 1988 when he was a sophomore at Sogang University. The band received national attention when it appeared on the televised 1988 MBC Campus Music Festival, a singing competition for amateurs. Muhangwedo won first place for the song "To You" (그대에게) which was written by Shin.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-:2-7) The band released one album, 1989's _When Our Lives Are Almost Over_ (우리 앞의 생이 끝나갈 때).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-8)
texts.2:
Shin released his first solo album in 1990, which included a song that had an English rap, which was unconventional in the Korean music scene at the time. The album was a huge hit, leading to Shin rising to the top of Korean pop music charts and receiving multiple Korean pop music awards. His second solo album, _Myself_, was released in 1991, which was first album in Korea to have used midi. He also started a gig as a radio DJ on MBC FM.
In 1992, Shin formed the band N.EX.T — moving from pop music to rock. Their first album, _Home_, was a concept album. While his previous songs were mainly about love or heartache, here Shin started to write more about social issues, such as criticizing the fast lifestyle of urbanites in "City People". The group's second album was released in 1994 titled _The Return of N.EX.T Part 1: The Being_ where Shin introduced more philosophical lyrics, such as questioning the meaning of life in the song "The Ocean: About Immortality". The band's third album, _The Return of N.EX.T Part 2: World_. Some of the band members changed over time, with Shin being the constant lead singer/songwriter.
During this time he also did a one-time collaboration with singer Yoon Sang to form Nodance, wrote the original sound track for the Korean movie _Jungle Story_, and was the DJ for the MBC FM radio program _FM Music City_ from 1996 to 1997. In 1996, he created his own label, Big Bang Music.
In 1997 N.EX.T released a rock ballad single, "Here, I Stand for You" which sold 500,000 copies in South Korea. The band went on to release their fourth album _Lazenca: A Space Rock Opera_ in November 1997, which was also the original sound track for the television animation series _Lazenca_. The band split up after this- Shin went on to study music producing in London.
texts.3:
In London, Shin re-named himself Crom (inspired by Cromwell) and released a techno album _Crom's Techno Works_ in 1998. The following year, he formed a project group Monocrom with guitarist Chris Tsangarides and released the eponymous project album _Monocrom_. The music in the album was experimental, combining heavy metal with Korean folk music, rap, and lyrical rock ballads. Most of the songs in this album were in English, which he collaborated with lyricist D. Yvette Wohn. After the release of _Monocrom_, Shin went to New York where he worked on producing his live album and some Korean movie soundtracks. In 2000, he created a three-man band Wittgenstein to produce a home studio album of the same name. He also wrote the song "Zergs are Coming" for the StarCraft music album.
Shin returned to Korea in 2002 and worked on various projects, mainly writing songs for other artists or for movie soundtracks. In 2004, he re-formed the group N.EX.T although the members were different, and released a double album _The Return of N.EX.T Part 3: 개한민국_. He also started DJing for a late night radio show _Ghost Nation_ that became extremely popular. In 2007, N.EX.T released a jazz album _The Songs for the One_ inspired by his newborn daughter. In 2008, the band released the album _666 Trilogy_. After a long break, the band's final album, _Reboot Myself_ was released in 2014.
In 2004, Shin participated in a special project with the best musicians of Korea, an album named "Tribute to Park Nohae's Collection of poems _The Dawn of Labor_ 20th anniversary".[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin_Hae-chul#cite_note-10) It is the first attempted project in the history of Korean music with recordings dedicated to poetry. Shin sang "Heaven" (하늘) with Psy on this album.
